key_insight: Local flow splitting and merging in disordered porous media create a pore-scale flow-rate distribution that is Gamma-shaped and topologically constrained by the network geometry.
engineering_relevance: The model enables fast prediction of flow heterogeneity in porous materials from minimal geometric information, which is useful for filtration, reactive transport, and permeability design.
method: Built a pore-network model for steady Stokes flow in 2D disordered arrays of circular obstacles.
Derived the pore-body flow-rate distribution as a Gamma distribution and related throat flows to it through local flow correlations.
Linked the Gamma parameters to simple geometry, especially the coefficient of variation of pore throat widths.
evidence_signal: The theory agrees closely with computational fluid dynamics simulations and outperforms prior mean-field models that ignore local flow-rate correlations.
watch_item: The framework is developed for steady 2D Stokes flow in disordered obstacle arrays, so care is needed when extending it to inertial, transient, or strongly three-dimensional porous flows.
paper_title: Topological origin of flow distributions in disordered porous media
